correctness.rationale: After normalization, the sampled squared modulus is a concave quadratic in the sampled cosine. The candidate puts its vertex at the midpoint of the two cosine samples adjacent to zero. A weighted two-sample lower bound has a strictly positive-definite Hessian on the coefficient simplex; its stationarity conditions are exactly the balancing identity and the strictly monotone quartic equation. This proves global optimality on the stated sign face for every odd modulus. The asymptotic follows from Taylor expansion of the unique root. The finite verifier only corroborates these analytic identities.

value.rationale: The Newman sign face is canonically selected by the classical continuous extremizer rather than by an arbitrary parameter slice. The theorem gives an all-odd-modulus exact optimization, explicit extremizing magnitudes, a convex certificate, and a sharp second-order lower bound for the unresolved unrestricted odd finite-grid problem. It quantifies how allowing the classical extremizer's magnitudes to retune to the odd grid changes the finite sampling gain.
